about: The epistola of the formulary “16th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: I entreat you not to falter in my tribulations for you, which is your glory. On this account I bend my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, from whom every fatherhood in the heavens and on earth is named, that He may give you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with might through His Spirit for the inner man, and that Christ may dwell by faith in your hearts; in order that you, rooted and founded in love, may be able to grasp what the breadth and the length and the loftiness and the depth are, together with all the saints, and to know also the love of Christ which surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled to the whole fullness of God. And to Him who can do all things far more abundantly than we ask or understand, according to the power that works within us, to Him be glory within the Church and in Christ Jesus, to all generations, for ever and ever. Amen.
